attributes.body_ja:
「ながらも」は、接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）「ながら」と副助詞（ふくじょし）「も」の組（く）み合（あ）わせです。漢字（かんじ）で書（か）くと「乍（なが）ら」になります。「ながら」は「その動作（どうさ）を続（つづ）けたままで」や「その状態（じょうたい）が続（つづ）いたままで」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）しますが、「ながらも」も「(A) だけれども、(B) だ」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「ながらも」はふつう、(A) と (B) が同時（どうじ）に成（な）り立（た）っていることに驚（おどろ）く気持（きも）ちを表（あらわ）します。イ形容詞（けいようし）、ナ形容詞（けいようし）、名詞（めいし）や動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。

「ながらも」は、(A) の状態（じょうたい）がそのまま続（つづ）いている中（なか）で (B) が起（お）こることを強調（きょうちょう）します。そのため、動作（どうさ）を表（あらわ）す動詞（どうし）ではなく、気持（きも）ちや性質（せいしつ）などの状態（じょうたい）を表（あらわ）す動詞（どうし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。
attributes.body:
ながらも is a combination of the conjunction particle ながら, and the adverbial particle も. Coming from the kanji 乍（なが）ら, with the meaning of 'while', ながら almost always keeps this nuance. Because of this, ながらも can be translated as 'even while (A), (B)', or 'although (A), also (B)'.

ながらも usually expresses surprise at the coexistence of (A) and (B), and may be used after い-Adjectives, な-Adjectives, nouns, or the conjunctive form of verbs.

ながらも is used to highlight a thing that comes after the existing state of (A) 'そのままで後（あと）に続（つづ）く事（こと）'. Due to this, ながらも may only be used with verbs that highlight states of existence (like feelings), rather than ongoing actions.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: にしても and ながらも both express contrast. にしても introduces something counter to the condition, e.g. 難しいにしてもやってみたほうがいい ('Even if it's hard, you should try doing it'). ながらも shows two opposing facts that coexist, e.g. 忙しいながらも楽しんでいる ('I'm busy, but still enjoying it').

attributes.body: Both express contrast, but with different nuances and usage. ながらも attaches to verbs, adjectives, or nouns and conveys contradictory states, e.g. '緊張しながらもわくわくしている' ('While feeling anxious, I'm also excited'). それなのに is used at the start of a sentence to mean 'and yet', often with surprise, e.g. '８時間も寝た。それなのに眠い' ('I slept eight whole hours. But still, I'm sleepy').

attributes.body: ながらも and にもかかわらず both express contradiction, but differ in nuance and usage. ながらも conveys coexisting contradictory states, e.g. '緊張しながらもわくわくしている' ('While feeling anxious, I'm also excited'). にもかかわらず means 'despite' and is used when something occurs against expectations, e.g. '雨にもかかわらず出かけた' ('He went out despite the rain').

second_relatable.title: にもかかわらず
second_relatable.meaning: Despite, In spite of, Regardless, Nevertheless

attributes.body: Both mean 'while' or 'although' and are often interchangeable, e.g. '何度も休みつつ、ゴールまでたどりついた' ('While/although resting many times, I neared the goal'). This could also be expressed as '何度も休みながらも...'. However, ながらも requires the action to occur over time, so '手紙を開きつつ' ('while opening the letter') would typically not use ながらも.

attributes.body: ながらも and くせに both express contradiction, but differ in nuance. ながらも simply expresses two seemingly contradictory states coexisting in a neutral fashion, e.g. 緊張しながらもわくわくしている ('While feeling anxious, I'm also excited.'). In contrast, くせに implies blame or criticism, e.g. 知っているくせに教えてくれない ('Even though he knows, he won't tell me.').

attributes.body: Both のに and ながらも express contrast, but with different focuses. のに is more general and used widely, like the English 'although.' ながらも is mainly used with state-expressing verbs and conveys surprise that something happened despite that state.
